purpose: Measure whether SAM2's existing three-mask initial prompt improves full-video indexed-position Lean propagation relative to its identical-prompt-schedule single-mask reference.
selection: Retrospective diagnostic cases chosen before any candidate video inference: seq3 engineering replay, seq8/11/20/23 user-requested difficult videos, seq13/18 initial-mask regressions, seq15/17 prior CPU repeat-order regressions. Not a representative or independent cohort.
candidate: Same archived first detector box, frame, CPU FP32, model, multiscale Lean 25% memory budget, and indexed spatial RoPE as the audited reference. Temporarily activate the author SAM2 multimask decoder for the box and feature-point initial prompts; rank by SAM2's predicted IoU as implemented by the author. Recompute feature points from the automatic candidate provisional mask, then pass its automatic refined mask to the original Lean memory initialization. Restore native multimask policy before all tracking. No re-detection or new runtime gating/threshold.
engineering: Reuse the two independent verified first-frame runs and their full 21-video label-free prompt study. Run the candidate video seq3 twice without labels, verify fixed model weights and prompt replay, no context leakage, reproducible mask and token-position/selection traces and compare against the indexed reference. Only then run the full diagnostic cohort, save every mask before scoring, and independently rescore candidate and indexed reference against the same labels. No labels enter inference.
limitations: First-frame mean Dice was essentially unchanged and all five initial labeled-empty false alarms persisted. Selected video outcomes are exploratory. GT-prompt native and Lean histories are unequal-initialization references. No per-sequence oracle selection or per-frame gating is used.
